presets.goal: "I have about 3 months of data — is my stablecoin yield strategy any good?"
presets.report:
VERDICT: INSUFFICIENT-EVIDENCE

What was tested — and how hard: your proposal was checked against 1 counted trial in its family (the ledger counts every iteration — that is the honest number of strategies searched, and it makes the statistical bar harder, not easier).

What it means: Not enough evidence to decide either way — only 90 observations against a power floor of 225. This is neither a yes nor a no; it is a "come back with more data" clock. (The floor itself is ASSUMED, pending an external audit — Rule XXXVIII.)

What could change it: More point-in-time observations (currently 90 of an assumed 225 needed). The clock runs forward; there is no promise it will ever clear.

What could still go wrong even if this were positive: past-data significance is not a promise of future return; the point-in-time data, the survivorship of the venues, and the search you did NOT declare are all risks the engine cannot see. A verdict here is a floor on doubt, not a guarantee.
presets.teaches: Not enough evidence yet is a forward clock, not a failure — the engine tells you how much more it needs.

presets.goal: "I tried 8 versions of my strategy and the last one looks great — approve it?"
presets.report:
VERDICT: NO-GO

What was tested — and how hard: your proposal was checked against 8 counted trials in its family (the ledger counts every iteration — that is the honest number of strategies searched, and it makes the statistical bar harder, not easier).
Deflated significance at 8 trials: 0.947 (the bar is 0.95).

What it means: No edge found: what looked promising did not survive an honest correction for how many strategies were tried. This is the expected outcome for most proposals and is not a failure of the tool.

What could change it: A genuinely different mechanism, pre-registered before its out-of-sample window and re-derived on the engine's own data. Iterating the same idea will NOT help — every attempt is counted and makes the bar harder.

What could still go wrong even if this were positive: past-data significance is not a promise of future return; the point-in-time data, the survivorship of the venues, and the search you did NOT declare are all risks the engine cannot see. A verdict here is a floor on doubt, not a guarantee.
presets.teaches: Iterating to look better makes the bar harder: the ledger counted all 8 tries and deflated the score. Cherry-picking is impossible here.
